web.description:
## Cache Components in Next.js
Learn use cache, cacheLife, and cacheTag, and why data is dynamic by default.

Caching was on by default and mostly invisible in your code.

Cache Components, introduced in Next.js 16, flips that default.

## Setting a lifetime with cacheLife
```js
cacheLife({ stale: 300, revalidate: 900, expire: 3600 });
```

## What you no longer need
| No longer needed | What you use instead |
|-|-|
| `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` | Nothing, dynamic is the default |

## Key Takeaways
- **Cache Components flips the default.** With `cacheComponents: true`, data is dynamic by default and you opt into caching with `"use cache"`.

## [cacheLife(): Time-Based Revalidation](https://vercel.com/academy/nextjs-foundations/cache-components#cachelife-time-based-revalidation) ``` import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const config: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, // Enable Next.js 16.3 Instant Navigations cacheLife: { // Blog posts - longer cache, updates are rare blog: { stale: 3600, // 1 hour fresh revalidate: 86400, // 24 hours before revalidation expire: 604800, // 1 week max before forced regeneration }, // Product catalog - moderate cache products: { stale: 300, // 5 minutes fresh revalidate: 900, // 15 minutes before revalidation expire: 3600, // 1 hour max }, // Real-time data - minimal cache social: { stale: 60, // 1 minute fresh revalidate: 300, // 5 minutes before revalidation expire: 600, // 10 minutes max }, }, } export default config ``` ## [Decision Framework](https://vercel.com/academy/nextjs-foundations/cache-components#decision-framework) ``` I'm implementing Cache Components in Next.js 16 and need help deciding on a caching strategy. Next.js 16 Cache Components offer: - `"use cache"` directive for shared caching - `"use cache: private"` for per-user caching - `cacheLife()` for time-based expiration (profiles: blog, products, social, etc.) - `cacheTag()` + `updateTag()` for immediate mutation visibility - `cacheTag()` + `revalidateTag(tag, 'max')` for stale-while-revalidate refreshes **Data type:** _____ Example: "Product catalog", "User dashboard", "Blog posts", "Live sports scores" **How often it changes:** _____ Example: "Every few hours", "When admin updates", "Real-time", "Once a day" **Is it user-specific?** - [ ] Same for all users (shared) - [ ] Different per user (personalized) **Staleness tolerance:** _____ Example: "5 minutes is fine", "Must be real-time", "1 hour acceptable" **What triggers updates:** _____ Example: "Admin publishes", "User makes purchase", "External API webhook" ```tsx // My current data fetching: ___PASTE_YOUR_DATA_FETCHING_CODE___ ``` **Questions:** 1. Should I cache this data at all? 2. Which cacheLife profile fits? (blog, products, social, or custom) 3. Should I use time-based (cacheLife) or mutation-based (cacheTag) invalidation? 4. Shared cache or per-user cache? Generate a complete caching implementation with the appropriate directives and invalidation strategy. Explain why each choice fits my data. ``` ## [Troubleshooting](https://vercel.com/academy/nextjs-foundations/cache-components#troubleshooting) ``` import { connection } from 'next/server' export default async function Page() { await connection() // Opts into dynamic rendering const timestamp = Date.now() // Now allowed return

Generated at {timestamp}

} ``` ## [Solution](https://vercel.com/academy/nextjs-foundations/cache-components#solution) ``` import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const config: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, // Enable Next.js 16.3 Instant Navigations cacheLife: { blog: { stale: 3600, // 1 hour revalidate: 86400, // 24 hours expire: 604800, // 1 week }, products: { stale: 300, // 5 minutes revalidate: 900, // 15 minutes expire: 3600, // 1 hour }, social: { stale: 60, // 1 minute revalidate: 300, // 5 minutes expire: 600, // 10 minutes }, }, } export default config ```
